prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Modes (Airport Duty Manager=ADM declares; Business Rules Registry gives thresholds/latency targets): Normal Operations; Adverse Weather(surface advisories weighted higher); Capacity Reduction State(ADM+Tower Supervisor extend metering horizon; RFM may combine arrival regulation+departure metering); Recovery Phase(Copperfin-approved; RFM authorizes exit; remove multi-rotation surface holds first); Contingency Fallback; Slot Compliance State; Winter(MBO confirms in Digital Briefing Room; CAM cuts departure capacity). Actors: Regional Flow Manager(RFM; staged rate increase after Ironleaf confirms spacing; uses advisories to choose normal sequencing/local metering/Tactical Regulation Proposal), Airspace Sector Planner(Sector Load Monitor), Military Airspace Liaison, Tower Supervisor(runway meters; Quartzline pad releases), ADM(surface-constraint significance in Foxglove; sets stand recovery priority favoring multi-conflict removal), Ramp Control Lead(verifies equipment-outage scope; coordinates stand reopening with Ground Handling Dispatcher), Aircraft Operator Rep, Airline Operations Coordinator(keep/new TOBT or later CTT; uses Gate Reopening Memo), Slot Coordinator(CTT vs surface release), Network Operations Liaison, Emergency Response Coordinator, Deicing Coordinator, Ground Handling Dispatcher, Meteorology Briefing Officer=MBO. Halcyon logs push rationale. Cedarbell=Regional Flow Platform(correlates surface equipment with flight intent/stand/runway). Parts: Integrated Tactical Management Position; Marlinstone=Demand Prediction Service(Flight Intent Messages; regulation when demand>Airport Acceptance Rate); CAM=Capacity Assessment Module; Blueharbor=Slot Allocation Engine(CTT, Ground Delay Program, Pushback Window Token); Foxglove=Airport CDM Portal(gate conflicts: flights, connection exposure, size compatibility, latest feasible off-block); Emberline=Departure Metering Service(pushback spacing→Blueharbor; CTT→Ironleaf=Tower Sequence Manager); North/South Runway Meters; Surface Surveillance Adapter(→Ramp Movement Board, Ironleaf); Ramp Movement Board(apron advisories; stand timeline: occupied/blocked/cleaning/boarding/tow-ready); Gate Conflict Detector(tries adjacent-stand resequencing before broader delay; compares arrivals, departures, gates, towing, stand status); Handling Resource Planner(extra resources vs flow measure); Lantern(distributes surface/apron advisories to subscribed roles within latency); Common Situation

New part:
S474: The Surface Surveillance Adapter verifies that the apron position is physically clear, while the East Apron Sensor and West Apron Sensor provide supporting movement evidence for the reopened area.
S475: The Tower Supervisor is advised only when the gate or stand decision changes runway sequence assumptions, expected taxi duration, or a departure metering commitment.
S476: The Aircraft Operator Representative confirms whether the aircraft can accept a revised stand assignment without disrupting maintenance release, fueling sequence, boarding control, or cabin readiness.
S477: The Handling Resource Planner estimates whether the proposed turnaround can be recovered using available loading teams, passenger stairs, boarding bridges, cleaning crews, and baggage transfer resources.
S478: The Airline Interface Adapter maintains airline-provided connection exposure, including protected passengers, minimum connection time pressure, and groups that require assisted transfer.
S479: The Regional Flow Manager balances passenger connection pressure against network fairness when a gate recovery action would improve one bank of departures but consume scarce apron capacity.
S480: The Network Operations Liaison reviews whether protecting a connecting passenger group supports wider network recovery or only transfers delay to a later sector.
S481: The Slot Coordinator protects constrained rotations by checking that a recovered gate plan remains compatible with the applicable Calculated Takeoff Time and any slot compliance expectation.
S482: The Target Off Block Time is revised only when the actor responsible for the turnaround confirms that the boarding, servicing, and ramp movement assumptions are achievable.
S483: The Departure Metering Service sequences recovered departures so that aircraft released from delayed turnarounds do not create a new surface queue at the runway holding points.
S484: Sector Load Monitor produces the Departure Fix Load Sheet when projected recovered departures require a consolidated view of demand by departure fix.
S485: The Airport CDM Portal shows downstream departure-fix pressure as contextual information for gate recovery decisions, without allowing the stand plan to override accepted airspace constraints.
S486: The Business Rules Registry holds the local rules for connection protection, gate compatibility, towing priority, stand reopening approval, and minimum turnaround recovery margins.
S487: The Collaborative Decision Log records each accepted conflict resolution with the chosen stand, rejected alternatives, affected passenger connections, and the rationale used by the responsible actor.
S488: The Audit Event Ledger preserves the same decision history for later traceability, including manual overrides, timestamp corrections, and identity of the approving role.
S489: The Performance Analytics Warehouse measures whether recovered gate assignments reduced missed connections, reduced secondary stand conflicts, and improved aircraft rotation stability during the Recovery Phase.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
